open_decision: The order of the new rows after the old registry rows: the laws fix the set and the count of the new rows, but not their order.
input: enable = false, locked = anything, registry r = [], starter list st = [{id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}, {id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}] (ids are distinct, so the list is legal)
result_a: [{id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}, {id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}] (the design ref: new rows in starter order)
result_b: [{id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}, {id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}] (a design that reverses the new rows)
reason: Each law talks about membership, length, or the old prefix of the result, so a design that appends the same new rows in reverse order passes every law. The two designs give different registries for this input.
